title: pool-coverage-heatmap-scenario-runbook
summary: Working workbook and runbook for generating coverage vs. commit heatmaps across reserved GPU pools. Purpose: give product + finance a repeatable sim to recommend tranche sizes, rollover windows, and spot/priority mixes that hit X% coverage targets while minimizing expected idle cost.
key_assumptions: 1) Demand arrivals modeled by per-customer hourly Poisson with seasonal multiplier derived from historical qps slices; 2) Job size distribution bootstrapped from 6 months of observed run lengths (heavy tail); 3) Rollover behavior: customers with >=90% usage renew at 80% probability; 4) Spot preemption risk mapped to 10/30/60 minute interruption windows depending on cloud region; 5) Spot discount assumed between 25-55% depending on instance family.
methodology: Monte Carlo simulation over 10k trials per scenario. For each trial: sample hourly demand curve, allocate reserved commitments first, fill remainder with on-demand (high cost) and spot (discounted but possibly preempted). Track metrics: coverage probability (percent of hours demand <= capacity), expected idle (mean unused GPU-hours), 95th shortfall (hours with demand exceeding capacity), blended unit cost (USD per GPU-hour after discounts). Heatmap aggregates scenarios by commit tranche on X axis and spot allowance on Y axis.
model_outputs: coverage_pct: probability that reserved+spot capacity meets demand per-hour
expected_idle_pct: fraction of reserved capacity unused on average
blended_unit_cost_usd: amortized cost per GPU-hour including reserved amortization and spot/on-demand fill
95pct_shortfall_gph: 95th percentile of shortfall in GPU-hours when demand exceeds capacity
optimal_rollover_window: recommended commit rollover length to smooth demand mismatches
sensitivity_delta: marginal change in blended cost when +/- 10% demand
top_level_recommendations: Introduce a 3-tranche commit offering (Small/Medium/Large) pegged to 30/120/360 GPU-months with explicit spot-allowance bands at 20/35/50%. Improves coverage curve curvature and simplifies sales conversations.
Set default rollover window to 60 days with an early-exit penalty sliding scale to discourage short-term gaming — reduces churn-driven coverage spikes by estimated 6%.
Offer a 25% spot-discount product with a hard preemption SLA for enterprise customers (priority burst option) to move mid-tail demand off on-demand and into cheaper buckets.
Pilot dynamic commit top-ups (API-triggered add-on purchases) during predictable seasonal windows to avoid permanent overcommitment.
Add a daily automated report (heatmap snapshot + top 3 sensitivity deltas) to the Console for Dedicated customers to encourage self-optimization.
